The author source reaches its final boundary from AutonomousMode.SubState3, while the closed model introduces FinalWaittr_0005 and gives that synthetic boundary outgoing human-steering and Power_Off exits; the target/ancestor continuation therefore does not close stable termination.
candidates.expected: The system should terminate at the final state on Power Off and have no continuation from the designated termination target or its active ancestors.
candidates.observed: The authored completion edge maps from SubState3 to a synthetic FinalWaittr_0005 state, and that state has reachable outgoing transitions for the human-steering event and Power_Off; AutonomousMode also has continuation transitions to HumanDrivingMode and root completion.
candidates.reason: Endpoint existence does not establish stable termination. The exact designated completion path has active continuation from the synthetic target and enclosing AutonomousMode.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The source's [*] notation denotes completion and the synthetic state is compiler-owned, so the extra continuations may be lowering artifacts rather than authored termination behavior; the closed model nevertheless exposes them as active continuation carriers.
candidates.title: Final State Is Not Stablely Terminal

arguments.reason: The closed model contains an unconditional root initial edge to HumanDrivingMode, but the edge is triggered by Power_On and is therefore not an unconditional owner-default entry. Power_On has a declared consumer with no reachable consumer. The required endpoint transitions for autonomous state, human driving mode, and final state are present in the author-source inventory and represented by closed-model macro roots, while the designated final state in the source is reached through an authored completion edge whose closed model continues through a synthetic boundary and allows further event-driven exits; termination therefore remains a distinct issue. HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode are declared and root-reachable, and AutonomousMode contains the authored substate structure.

issues.expected: On Power Off, the system should transition to the required final state.
issues.observed: Power_Off exits exist from HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode to [*] completion boundaries; no unique closed state ref represents the normative final state.
issues.reason: Completion-boundary equivalence is plausible but not uniquely typed as a final-state endpoint.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The authored [*] notation denotes completion and the closed model preserves corresponding root completion exits.
issues.title: Power-Off Final-State Endpoint Identity

issues.basis: NL5 assigns stable termination to final state; the authored completion path reaches compiler-owned FinalWaittr_0005, which has reachable event-driven continuations, while AutonomousMode also has continuations.
issues.expected: The system should terminate at the final state on Power Off with no continuation from the target or active ancestors.
issues.observed: FinalWaittr_0005 has reachable human-steering and Power_Off exits, and AutonomousMode has continuation exits to HumanDrivingMode and root completion.
issues.reason: Endpoint existence does not establish stable termination; the designated target and active ancestor retain continuation behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source final boundary and synthetic target may reflect compiler lowering, but the closed model exposes the continuations as active carriers.
